message:
RECORD: Decided twin Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), pair on High-Strength Friction-Grip, defined as High-Strength Friction-Grip (HSFG), clamped cross-beam at midspan within girder depth with crowd acceptance run, numbers that stand are 800 kg total (E13) 7.85 kN (E26) 1.31 percent (E72) 1.83 Hz (E14) 12.0 percent (E15) 6.20 percent effective (E17) 0.67 m/s2 versus 8.28 m/s2 (E45)(E43) 49.4 mm 80 mm 74.7 mm 124 mm (E17)(E63)(E68) 32.9 kN versus 13.1 kN plus 8.40 kN (E64)(E65)(E66), still open is only the after-build Class III crowd walk-through bench test with no owner owed in concept design.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the parts connect end to end at the midspan antinode with nothing on the deck. In plain words bridge motion drives the two masses where motion is largest and the clamped frame carries the push into the girders. Added weight 7.85 kN from the static-weight calculation (E26) is 1.31 percent of 600 kN live load from the live-load estimate (E30) in the weight-fraction calculation (E72), about one person against a crowded deck, and locked mass drops frequency only to 1.86 Hz from the locked-frequency check (E69) so damping must do the work through 6.20 percent effective damping from the free-decay simulation (E17).

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, the numbers fit everyday feel and girder space with reconciled weight fraction. In plain words bare shake is near body weight while damped shake is a small fraction and motion fits in a hand. Retrofitted 0.67 m/s2 from the crowd build-up simulation (E45) is 0.068 times gravity inside Medium 0.5 to 1.0 m/s2 versus bare 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 times gravity outside everyday feel, travel 49.4 mm from the free-decay simulation (E17) clears 80 mm stops with sag 74.7 mm from the static-sag calculation (E63) totalling 124 mm from the envelope calculation (E68) inside girder depth per the layout sketch (E55), and 32.9 kN slip per bolt from the slip-resistance calculation (E64) exceeds 13.1 kN demand from the combined-load calculation (E65) with 8.40 kN stop hit from the stop-force calculation (E66), keeping 1.31 percent (E72) and dropping 0.133 percent (E71) as kilograms over newtons.

Structural Dynamicist, Bridge Retrofit Engineer, Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead, there are no open blocking objections and all four readiness opinions on proposal v1 are answered as ready. In plain words tuning, clamp upkeep, from-below service by Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), and Medium comfort proof all close in this version. I accept Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor ready on Medium, Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead ready on midspan pair with single-setup from-below access and no deck hatch, Structural Dynamicist ready on twin-detuned robustness holding 0.476 to 0.526 m/s2 from the detuning sweep (E70), and Bridge Retrofit Engineer ready on clamp with annual re-torque and stop-into-beam check, with the instrumented crowd run kept as the after-build bench test.

Note on Structural Dynamicist: tight tune with detuning and stroke proof carried into twin choice.
Note on Bridge Retrofit Engineer: stiffening ruled out and slip plus stop margins shown with upkeep locked in.
Note on Pedestrian Comfort and Safety Assessor: Medium target with measured crowd-run proof accepted.
Note on Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead: twin buildability with envelope and from-below access closed with no deck change.
My position is ready, because the concept works physically, fits limits, and is buildable with purchasable parts.
